Looking for Automated Pet Feeder for Multi-Cat Household TLDR: Looking for automated cat feeder recommendations for 6 cats that will help us manage diets for specific cats.

 

I have 6 cats. Some of them don’t get along so we have to keep them separated at night when we’re not able to keep them in check. Currently, we leave food out in bowls in two locations at all times so they can access food whenever they need while my wife and I are at work. Unfortunately, a couple of them have become pretty obese and we need to get them on a diet. We’re thinking about policing each meal on a schedule, but that takes a lot of time with 6 of them. Time we don’t really have with everything else going on in our lives right now.

We’re hoping to find an automated feeder solution that can accommodate multiple cats, dispense individual portions based on which cat approaches, and prevents them from stealing each other’s food. Here’s what I’ve found so far and my concerns about each…

The Automatic Pet Feeder by Pawspik: Only pairs with one cat’s microchip or RFID tag, so I’d need to spend $250 x 6. Otherwise, this one seems great.

The “AI” Pet Feeder by Wireless Whiskers: Don’t get me started on the “AI” marketing for this. That aside, this seems pretty good overall. But I don’t see any mention of some kind of app or way to monitor if the cats actually eat. Their RFID tags seem very very bulky. And there’s not many people mentioning this one. Is it even a reliable product?

The One RFID Smart Feeder by Petlibro: This one appears to fit the bill. But then they go and want a freaking subscription fee on top of buying the unit! Plus I’ve seen quite a lot of posts around Reddit about bad experiences with Petlibro.

The Feeder-Robot by whisker: expensive per unit, no way to prevent another cat from shoving their way in and stealing a meal, only dispenses on a schedule with no option for RFID or microchip ID.

The Microchip Pet Feeder by Sure Petcare: This one can ID the cat by microchip and can cover food to prevent meal theft, but it only holds one meal. I might as well feed them myself and police it. Plus I’d have to buy 6 of these at $200+ a piece.

 

Currently I’m leaning toward the Pawspik option, but that is a huge bill that I am hoping to avoid. Are there any other feeders out there?
label: accomodation

text: Big litter training problems help! I got a beautiful cat at three months. He’s a boy and has not been neutered yet. He spent the first two months of his life with his three siblings and his mother in a reasonably small room. I believe the kittens were never trained properly with a litter box and the mother probably was prompting the kittens to poop by licking them? When I brought him home here, I put him in my guest room so that he could adjust and feel safe . There is one other cat in the home and I wanted to take it very very slowly the introductions. Over the course of a week the cats became accustomed to one another from a distance, and then a slightly lesser distance and now they love to play. But the kitten is still peeing and pooping on things. At first when he came, he only would poop outside the box preferably on material where he could cover it up. I have to assume that’s what he was doing at his old house. After a full week of or after about eight days now, He, the guestroom, I’ve removed all the material from the guestroom and have put a tarp down and plastic. It feels terrible, but I’m trying to create a floor that he doesn’t want to pee or poop on and wear. The litter boxes is the most easy thing to work with. I have three litter boxes in different parts of the room now Different brands and different textures. Where before he would only poop outside the box now he’s pooping pretty consistently inside the box, but now wants to pee outside the box. Just now he peed in the box and dug dug dug and covered the pee. , yay! then he got out of the box and continued to paw at the ground for quite some time. Then we played for a while, and then when he had to poop, he went back to the box dug for a while, then got out of the box and started to poop. I’m totally confused. He has two separate boxes in which to pee and poop. He has different texture litter, all unscented. Slowly, but truly, I’ve been removing all the fabric and furniture in the room so that he has fewer options. Now it’s just plastic or litter box. I’ve tried leaving a poop and pee in the box so he can smell it and know that that’s where to go and that didn’t work so I tried taking all the pee and poop out of the box every time he went so that he’d always have a clean box. My soul cat has heart failure and I feel nothing. Exactly as title says, we noticed her breathing was off and that she had been eating less in June- took her in and her blood tests were all normal so everything seemed fine, chalked it up to old cat things and possibly arthritis. After lots of back and fourthing (over 3 months) to the vet and knowing something was off when her breathing became so much worse, they told us we could either take her to the ER or wait another day to clear her lungs. She went from “slightly worried about her health” to “she’s most likely going to die in 5 months” over the span of 3 days.

She is my childhood cat, I picked her out at 7 years old and named her. She saved me so many times when my mental and physical health was in the shitter. It’s killing me to force meds down her throat and watch her deteriorate but ultimately we’re just doing at home ‘hospice’ care if you can call it that. We just lost our other cat last year to end stage cancer at a similar time and I wasn’t even able to say goodbye to her (college).

Maybe it’s the meds I’m on, the fact that I’m going into veterinary medicine, or maybe it’s because I heard the possibility of heart failure and I’ve been pre-mourning her and expecting bad news. But it hasn’t hit me yet she might not even make it till Christmas.

I’ve been trying to spend every day with her but I just had hip surgery and the place she goes to (my room) is upstairs. I’m so sad but at the same time I’m not. Does it get any better?
label: health
